summary: Apple's AI features clear a key Chinese approval with Alibaba's help, DeepSeek recovers from a five-hour outage, and economists expect Q3 growth near 4.4% ahead of official data.
body: Apple Intelligence, the iPhone's set of AI tools, moved closer to launching in China. China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology updated device permits so iPhones, including the new iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, can use Alibaba's Qwen language models and its Tongyi Wanxiang image and video generator [^1]. China limits foreign AI services, so Apple relies on local partners, and officials must also approve future model updates [^2]. Bloomberg, as reported by MacRumors, says the first version will be basic, with photo editing but no AI Siri or Image Playground [^2].

DeepSeek, the Chinese AI lab whose chatbot is widely used in China, had an outage on Thursday. Problems began at 8:11 a.m. Beijing time and affected its website, app and API (the connection other software uses to reach its models) [^3][^4]. All services were back by 1:04 p.m. The company said it found the cause but did not say what it was [^3].

On household money: e-bikes, a main way many Chinese people get around cities, sold 9% more in the third quarter than a year earlier, the first rise this year, according to research firm AVC. But in early October authorities suspended safety certificates for many models after failed factory checks, and Caixin reports sales have nearly stalled [^5]. Bank lending in September beat forecasts, while household borrowing stayed roughly flat after two months of shrinking, central bank data show [^7]. Official third-quarter growth figures have not come out yet; economists surveyed by Caixin expect about 4.4%, with September retail sales up only about 1% [^6]. My read: a quiet-ish day, with exports still carrying an economy where shoppers remain cautious.
differences: Timing of Apple's China AI launch differs. The South China Morning Post says Apple has confirmed an October launch [^1], while Bloomberg, as reported by MacRumors, says the features will arrive with iOS 27.3, expected in December [^2]. A test version in October and a wider release in December could both be true, but this is not confirmed.

reads.title: China's white-collar experts are training AI to pay the bills
reads.summary: From September: lawyers, teachers and engineers in China take gig work writing hard problems for AI models, often earning 100 to 500 yuan per task, as job markets tighten.
